newsitem.title: INDIA: Bangladesh PM hopeful of Ganges pact with India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM hopeful of Ganges pact with India.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Wednesday that she hoped to reach an agreement with India on the sharing Ganges River water that could prove crucial to her political future.
Hasina told reporters after a ceremonial reception at the Presidential Palace in New Delhi that she could not give details until bilateral talks were over.
"Discussions are going on. So I think after everything is settled, then we can say," she said.
Asked if she expected to finalise agreements with India by the end of her three-day visit on Thursday, she said: "I am hopeful."
The sharing of disputed Ganges water, crucial to the economies of both India and Bangladesh, is considered a major political test for Hasina.
The Ganges river flows through northern India before emptying into the Bay of Bengal in Bangladesh.
Dhaka says India holds back water during the annual January-June dry season and releases excessive quantities during monsoon rains, causing flooding.

Hasina met Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral in the Presidential Palace after being received by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who was scheduled to host a dinner for the visiting leader on Wednesday.

She was also scheduled to meet President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Vice President K.R. Narayanan, Congress party leader Sitaram Kesri, and Atal Behari Vajpayee, leader of the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
She was also expected to call on Sonia Gandhi, the widow of assassinated prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and who wields considerable influence in Indian politics.
Delegations from the two countries were to meet at 7 p.m. (1330 GMT). They were expected to sign a water-sharing agreement on Thursday before Hasina leaves India.
Hasina arrived in India on Tuesday and spent her first day in the western state of Rajasthan, where she offered prayers at a revered Moslem saint's tomb in Ajmer city.
